title: Listening Section 2 - Museum Tour Introduction
instruction: You will hear a guide giving an introductory talk to a group of visitors at a maritime museum. Answer Questions 1-10.

transcript.speaker: Jenny
transcript.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Harbour Maritime Museum. My name's Jenny and I'll be your guide today. Before we begin the tour, let me give you some background and a few practical points.

transcript.speaker: Jenny
transcript.text: The museum opened in nineteen eighty-five in what used to be the old customs house. At first it had only two rooms, but today there are six galleries spread over three floors.

transcript.speaker: Jenny
transcript.text: Tickets are normally nine pounds, but as you're a group, you've all been given the group price of seven pounds. Please keep your ticket with you, because you may be asked to show it in some galleries.

transcript.speaker: Jenny
transcript.text: Now, a word about what you can see. The ground-floor whaling gallery is closed for repairs until next month, so I'm afraid we'll have to miss that one. Some people think the shipwreck gallery is also closed because of the flooding last year, but it reopened in May, and we'll visit it later.

transcript.speaker: Jenny
transcript.text: If you'd like refreshments, the cafe is on the top floor, next to the terrace. Older leaflets say it's on the ground floor, but it moved two years ago. The gift shop is near the exit, so you can visit it at the end of your tour.

transcript.speaker: Jenny
transcript.text: You're welcome to take photographs, but please don't use flash in Gallery 3, where the old maps are kept. The light can damage the paper.

transcript.speaker: Jenny
transcript.text: Our free talk about the history of the harbour begins at half past eleven in Gallery 2. It lasts about twenty minutes, so you'll have time for it before lunch.

transcript.speaker: Jenny
transcript.text: Many visitors think that the most popular exhibit is the huge anchor in the entrance hall, and it is certainly the most photographed. But if you ask our staff, they'll tell you that visitors spend longest at the model of the ship Aurora. It was built by hand over eleven years.

transcript.speaker: Jenny
transcript.text: Finally, if you hear the fire alarm, please don't use the lifts. Follow the green signs to the nearest stairs and gather in the car park at the back of the building. Don't go back to the entrance, because the fire engines will arrive there.

transcript.speaker: Jenny
transcript.text: Right, if there are no questions, let's make a start in Gallery 1.
